Article Title: 'No NCP merger talks': Maharashtra minister Bharne after meeting Sunetra Pawar
Article Text:
Maharashtra minister Dattatray Bharne denies NCP merger talks at meeting with Sunetra Pawar, says discussion focused on drought situation and constituency work

NEW DELHI: There were no talks regarding the merger of the two Nationalist Congress Party (NCP) factions during the meeting of MLAs with deputy chief minister Sunetra Pawar, said maharashtra minister Dattatray Bharne on Friday."There was no party meeting or any political discussion on the merger. The party has not called any such meeting. Some of us happened to be here and met Sunetra Pawar. The discussion was mainly about the drought situation and the work that needs to be undertaken in our respective constituencies," news agency PTI quoted him as saying. Ajit Pawar , who was serving as Maharashtra's deputy chief minister, died in a plane crash in January this year.Following his death, his wife Sunetra Pawar took over as the NCP chief and assumed the post of deputy chief minister. Since then, speculation has persisted over a possible merger between the two NCP factions.The merger discussions gathered momentum last week after several leaders from the Sunetra Pawar-led NCP, including Praful Patel and Parth Pawar, held a meeting with NCP (SP) chief Sharad Pawar.Sunetra Pawar added to the speculation during a press conference in Baramati two days ago, saying that the situation would become clear at the appropriate time.
Article Summary: Dattatray Bharne denies NCP merger talks at meeting with Sunetra Pawar. Says discussion focused on drought situation and constituency work. Ajit Pawar, who was serving as Maharashtra's deputy chief minister, died in a plane crash in January this year.

NEW DELHI: Several suspects have been detained for questioning following the terror attack on a Central Reserve Police Force CRPF ) post in Jammu and Kashmir 's Kulgam district, in which three personnel were injured, officials told news agency PTI on Friday.Terrorists opened fire at the CRPF post in the south Kashmir district on Wednesday, triggering a massive cordon and search operation by security forces to track down the attackers.The search operation continued for the third consecutive day on Friday, with security forces maintaining a heightened vigil across the district. Barricades have been set up and armoured vehicles deployed at several locations.Vehicles are being stopped and frisked at security checkpoints as forces intensify surveillance in the area, officials said.Security agencies are also using human and technical intelligence to gather leads and track the terrorists. Several suspects have been picked up by police for questioning as part of the investigation, they added.Senior police officers and officials from other security agencies have visited the site of the attack to assess the situation and review security arrangements.Security has also been tightened across other parts of the Valley, with police and paramilitary personnel conducting random vehicle checks in Srinagar and other districts of Kashmir.

What prompted you to study law post-surrender?

Do you agree that the end of armed Naxalism is permanent and it will never resurrect?

After surrendering in Feb 2026 and enrolling in a law college, top CPI(Maoist) leader Thippiri Thirupathi alias Deoji, 61, is ready for his next innings in democratic politics. Deoji speaks to TOI's Bharti Jain on his demand to lift the ban on CPI(Maoist) and make it a lawful, people-centric party. Excerpts:Also read - 'From armed struggle to people's politics': Ex-Maoist leader Deoji outlines new path, seeks release of jailed cadres I left studies and shifted to Dandkarenya forests in 1984. The socio-political scenario in those times was marked by exploitation of peasantry and women by feudalistic set-up, both in urban and rural settings. In 1978, there was a big uprising by the farmers of Telangana and a declaration was made to fight against oppression and agitate for people's rights. There was mass mobilisation and a people’s movement started to give voice to farmers, women and the weaker sections. Starting from Karimnagar, it soon spread across Telangana. I was then following this movement closely and subscribed to its anti-feudal sentiment; I joined the students' Radical Students Union (RSU) to actively 'support this cause. I was arrested several times and tortured by the police. Since circumstances did not allow us to carry out our struggle in the open, I had to go underground.Our commitment to CPI(Maoist)’s agenda of seizing power through armed revolution, had mentally prepared us to face all odds and hardships. As we continued working, our resolve only strengthened...so negotiating difficult terrain, exhaustion, poor living conditions felt normal to us.There were three sources. Firstly, we would snatch or loot weapons (from the security forces); secondly, we manufactured weapons on our own. Thirdly, depending on the funds available, we also purchased arms and ammunition from the domestic arms dealers and smugglers. We have never secured weapons from anti-India, foreign-based sources in lieu of furthering their agenda.CPI(Maoist) was mostly funded by the people after we explained to them the political cause behind waging an armed struggle and the need for weapons. Also, we extorted money from outsiders who worked in our area; like tendu patta contractors and bamboo harvesters. But we steered clear of contractors engaged in construction of roads or bridges as we believe they exploit our resources. That CPI(Maoist) had massive funds is propaganda. Our policy is to raise money to sustain us for the next three years. This money is spent on people’s issues, armed struggle and propaganda; extravagance is strictly avoided. The party never had funds in excess of Rs 30-40 crore at any time. These would largely be exhausted after fulfilling needs for the current year; only a little would be carried over to the second year. There were never any funds for the third year.After People's War merged with MCC in 2004 to form the CPI(Maoist), then PM Manmohan Singh had declared Naxalism as the biggest internal security challenge facing the country. Thereafter, the entire govt machinery -- the Centre, affected states, intelligence agencies, Central para-military forces etc -- drafted a national policy to eradicate Naxalism. This unified, coordinated fight against Naxalism peaked in 2025. Security operations were only a part of this multi-pronged counter-Naxal approach, which also focused on a development of connectivity push in the affected areas. Many Naxals leaders, cadres and PLGA commanders were arrested or killed; we also lost our general secretary Namballa Keshav Rao in 2025. This weakened the CPI(Maoist) both quantitatively and qualitatively. Its geographical area of influence shrunk. We no longer had the capability to resist the security forces. Our weapons were seized. In view of our dwindling numbers, leadership, weaponry and area of influence, our movement suffered a massive setback.In Dec 2023, at an all-India conference of DGPs chaired by HM Amit Shah, consensus emerged in favour of waging a decisive battle to eliminate Naxalism. Operation Kagaar was launched in Jan 2024 and continued till March 2026.In Aug 2024, our PB/CC members met in Dandakaranya, We assessed that the decline in Naxals’ influence that began in 2018 had acquired serious proportions. We decided to disband the big outfits like PLGA, operate in small teams and work amongst the people. The cadres were incapable of implementing these decisions. It became too much of a security risk for them to move out of Dandakaranya. They had to concentrate there, exposing themselves to the forces that had encircled the area. We paid a heavy price as we could not operationalise the tactical decisions of Aug 2024.In March 2025, we decided that we were open to holding peace talks with the govt. Our condition was cessation of operations against us. But the Central govt rejected peace talks. The anti-Naxal operations continued with severity and many of our top leaders, including general secretary Nambala Keshav Rao, were killed. This crushed our movement. After Sonu surrendered, which was not cleared by PB, we could not arrest the wave of surrenders.Had the coordinated and fierce operations by the Centre and 12 states against CPI(Maoist) not been run with a definite deadline, our movement would have lasted longer as the people’s issues we raise remain relevant even today — loot by corporates in tribal areas and feudal oppression.Given the circumstances we did some rethinking and concluded that the situation was no longer conducive to continuing the armed struggle. So we decided to give up violence and come overground. We have not surrendered to lead a comfortable personal life. We want to take up people’s issues through legal means. We will now engage in people’s politics to achieve an oppression and exploitation-free society.We have been demanding that the ban on CPI(Maoist) should be lifted. This way we can take up political activity in an open and legal manner. Even the ban on our frontal outfits must go as there has been no violent incident from our side over the past 8-10 months.It is also our responsibility to secure the release of Maoist cadres languishing in prisons. This is our demand before the Centre and state govts. HM Amit Shah claims the country became Naxal-free in March 2026; so it is only apt to free Naxals who are still in jails. They cannot go back to violence when freed, as they don't have weapons. We welcome the govt’s decision to review cases against Naxals and free those jailed for non-serious crimes. But a distinction must not be drawn between serious and non-serious crimes. Govt may argue that the Maoists have killed many people, including police personnel, and that law should take its course. But this was a war and war always results in losses on both sides. After war, peace must be established. 6000-7000 Maoists are in jail; a blanket govt order must be issued for their release.Our third demand is leniency for the 10 Maoists given death sentence for the Jhiram Ghati attack case. Our demand for blanket release of Maoists should cover them as well.Our fourth demand is to extend protection to surrendered Naxals in Chhattisgarh against revenge attacks.Politics does not exist in a rigid form. Unlike Vedas, Puranas etc that are divine scriptures and cannot be rewritten, politics is dynamic. Politics must adapt to the changing times, be it the evolving national and international situation or objective and subjective conditions; political documents cannot be construed as eternal truth. Leninism and Marxism may be our theory, but the political document must be rewritten to reflect changed tactics and strategy.We will need to consult the other leaders as well as cadres of CPI(Maoist) on whether or not to join electoral politics. If the assessment is that elections will not achieve our ends, we may stay away.Since Shah had asked us to work openly and legally, our obvious choice is to do so through CPI(Maoist). We will wait and watch and take a call on alternatives if this does not work out.As we engage in political activity as per law, we shall need a network of legal experts across the country to implement our political agenda efficiently. The knowledge of law will help us to comment and correctly interpret the law to defend activities that are within the legal framework. It will also help in perception management.Armed struggle cannot be carried on or stopped with an edict or order. Popular sentiment decides its fate. Objective conditions create popular sentiment…which then takes the form of a call to the masses and congregation. This is how people’s movements are made. Nobody can predict what will happen in the future. But we are reiterating that after embracing a life in the open, we will carry out our political agenda only within the boundaries of the Constitution and law.
Article Summary: Former supreme commander and General Secretary of the banned CPI (Maoist), Thippiri Tirupathi, also known as Deoji, addresses media during a meeting with party leaders, in Hyderabad. Deoji speaks to TOI's Bharti Jain on his demand to lift the ban on CPI(Maoists) and make it a lawful, people-centric party.

Article Title: Indonesian woman with alleged Chinese links caught at Sonauli border after failing to speak Hindi
Article Text:
Indonesian woman held at Sonauli border with alleged forged Indian IDs; NGO links under investigation

LUCKNOW: An Indonesian woman, who allegedly posed as a Kolkata resident using forged Indian identity documents and claimed to be president of an NGO assisting Buddhist monks travelling to China, was caught by bureau of immigration officials at the Sonauli border in Maharajganj district after she was unable to speak Hindi properly during questioning.The woman, identified as Rohana, was intercepted on Nov 10 while attempting to cross into Nepal. She was allegedly carrying an Indian voter ID card, Aadhaar card and two PAN cards bearing different names and conflicting dates of birth. Her claimed association with a Kolkata-based NGO facilitating visits to China has emerged as a key aspect of the case.According to an FIR registered at Sonauli police station, the woman initially identified herself as Li Kim Lien, daughter of Li Chin Sen, and claimed to be a resident of New Tangra Road in Kolkata, West Bengal.The complaint lodged by immigration officer stated that the woman arrived at the Sonauli immigration office around 7.30 pm on Nov 10 and presented an Indian voter ID card bearing the number ZJJ2157469.The document identified her as Li Kim Lien, born on June 29, 1975, with a residential address at 8, New Tangra Road, under Kolkata Municipal Corporation, Tangra, Kolkata.However, immigration officials became suspicious when she was unable to speak Hindi properly.Her responses during questioning raised doubts about her claimed Indian identity, prompting officials to examine her passport.The passport, bearing number X2398351, identified her as Rohana, an Indonesian citizen born on Oct 20, 1970. It also showed that she possessed an Indian employment visa.The FIR states that she held an E-3 employment visa bearing number VL9126916, valid from Oct 11, 2025, to Nov 9, 2026. Her passport also contained details of a multiple-entry Indian visa issued on Aug 11, 2023.During questioning, the woman reportedly told immigration officials that she was working as president of an NGO based in Kolkata. She further claimed that the organisation provided technical assistance to Buddhist monks travelling to China.The FIR neither identifies the NGO nor specifies the nature of its activities or establishes any link with Chinese govt authorities."We are still in the initial stage of investigation to claim or deny if the woman was involved in espionage or any other activity beyond the alleged immigration and identity-document offences," an immigration official source said.According to the FIR, officials found that the woman possessed an Indian voter ID card, Aadhaar card and PAN card in the name of Li Kim Lien, while another PAN card was issued in the name of Rohana.The FIR alleges that the woman had obtained Indian identity documents by changing her name and address despite being an Indonesian citizen.Police registered the case under Sections 319(2), 336(3), 338 and 340(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, relating to cheating by personation, forgery and use of forged documents, along with Sections 22 and 23 of the Immigration and Foreigners Act, 2025.
Article Summary: Indonesian woman held at Sonauli border with alleged forged Indian IDs. She was allegedly carrying an Indian voter ID card, Aadhaar card and two PAN cards bearing different names and conflicting dates of birth. She claimed to be president of an NGO assisting Buddhist monks travelling to China.

Article Title: 2 SPOs killed in J&K’s Kishtwar, service rifles missing
Article Text:
2 SPOs killed in J&K’s Kishtwar, service rifles missing

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

JAMMU/SRINAGAR: Bullet-riddled bodies of two special police officers (SPOs) were found in the remote forests of J&K’s Kishtwar district Thursday, with their service rifles missing, triggering a search for the attackers and renewed concerns over a possible revival of terrorism in Chenab valley.Rashpal Kumar, 45, and Bobby Chand, 57, both residents of Kiyar Dachhan and posted with SOG Kiyar sector, had gone missing on Nov 10 while travelling to an Army post at Dharna-Marwah for rotation duty. A search was launched after they failed to reach the post. Their mobile phones were initially reachable but later switched off.One SPO had a bullet wound to his head and the other to his back. Their bodies were shifted for autopsy. Their INSAS and .303 rifles were missing.Sources said it was too early to link the killings to terrorism. However, Hizbul Mujahideen commander Jahangir Saroori, believed to be the longest-surviving terrorist in Chenab valley, was suspected to have been hiding in the area for decades. Mudassar, Riaj and south Kashmir terrorist Latif Bhat were also trying to revive terrorism in the region, the sources added.The killings came as security forces intensified searches in south Kashmir’s Kulgam after a terrorist fired at a CRPF checkpoint around 70km south of Srinagar Wednesday, wounding three personnel.A CRPF officer said the attack appeared to have been carried out by a lone gunman using a high-calibre weapon, possibly an AK-47, before escaping. The wounded men were out of danger.Political parties condemned both the Kulgam attack and the Kishtwar killings. J&K leader of opposition Sunil Sharma alleged terrorists had kidnapped the SPOs while they were travelling through the dense forest. “These terrorists, who are on the verge of being wiped out, are still trying to make their presence felt. This is a matter of concern for us,” he said.Former NC MP Aga Ruhullah Mehdi said the attacks were intended to derail the progress towards peace. “The perpetrators must be held accountable without delay,” he said.SPOs are temporary, honorarium-based local recruits appointed to assist J&K police. Trained in handling weapons, they support village defence committees, and participate in counter-terrorism operations alongside security forces in remote areas.In a separate operation in north Kashmir, security forces rounded up Ghulam Jeelani Reshi of Tangmarg from a forest. One hand grenade was found on him and another was found concealed in the forest following his disclosure, police said.
Article Summary: Rashpal Kumar, 45, and Bobby Chand, 57, had gone missing on Nov 10 while travelling to an Army post at Dharna-Marwah for rotation duty. A search was launched after they failed to reach the post. Their mobile phones were initially reachable but later switched off.

Article Title: Wangchuk under ‘house arrest’ as Ladakh rallies against hill council polls in winter
Article Text:
Wangchuk under ‘house arrest’

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

SRINAGAR: Leh Apex Body (LAB) member and climate activist Sonam Wangchuk was put under “house arrest” Thursday as an agitation began against a govt decision to hold Ladakh hill council polls on Dec 4 despite pleas to avoid the elections in the Union Territory (UT) during the harsh winter.Police removed Wangchuk from protest site NDS Memorial Park in Leh late Wednesday when he went there to oversee preparations, initially saying he “has been advised to stay at his residence”. Later, the Leh SSP issued formal “preventive” orders and restrictions on Wangchuk, saying his “activities, antecedents and alleged attempts to instigate the general public have affected public order before and there is an apprehension his future demonstrations may again lead to disturbance of peace”. “Dozens of armed guards surround my house,” Wangchuk posted late Thursday.A ban was clamped Wednesday on protests in view of the Dec 4 hill council polls and municipal/panchayat polls on Nov 21.Wangchuk and his LAB colleagues then issued an “SOS” appeal to President Droupadi Murmu, PM Narendra Modi and home minister Amit Shah to defer the polls. They cited the harsh winter and likely exclusion of many voters. LAB co-chairman Chering Dorjay Lakrook has said nearly 30% of the population is outside the region during winter.On Thursday, LAB said despite the crackdown and heavy deployment of security in Leh and Kargil, people from all walks of life participated in a peaceful dharna. “It sends a clear message to the administration that the people of Ladakh believe in peaceful and democratic means of protest and remain determined to raise their legitimate demands while exercising their constitutional right to protest, as guaranteed by the Constitution,” LAB said in a statement.Speaking at the protest site, Lakrook argued that LAB was not opposed to the hill council polls but holding them in winter would deprive a large number of people from voting. He also alleged that electoral rolls have been tampered with and Gen Z voters removed, calling it “Operation Lotus”.The elections follow an Oct 20 notification paving the way for hill councils in all eight districts in Ladakh, including newly created Sankoo. Ladakh earlier had two hill councils, one each in Leh and Kargil.Chief secretary Ashish Kundra has described the hill council polls as a “watershed moment” for Ladakh’s democracy. He has argued that schools remain open in the region till Dec 15 and if children can attend classes, there is no no reason adults can’t turn out to vote. The votes of both the hill council and panchayat polls will be counted on Dec 8.
Article Summary: Leh Apex Body member and climate activist Sonam Wangchuk was put under ‘house arrest’ Thursday. Police removed Wangchuk from protest site NDS Memorial Park in Leh late Wednesday when he went there to oversee preparations. A ban was clamped Wednesday on protests in view of the Dec 4 hill council polls and municipal/panchayat polls on Nov 21.

Article Title: 'I am under house arrest': Sonam Wangchuk speaks out against restrictions on movement in Ladakh
Article Text:
Sonam Wangchuk alleges he has been placed under house arrest without a formal order after Ladakh imposed 60-day movement restrictions on him

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Climate activist Sonam Wangchuk has written to the Ladakh administration seeking clarification over a 60-day order restricting his movement, alleging that he has effectively been placed under house arrest without any formal direction or legal justification.In his representation, dated November 12, Wangchuk said the order issued by the office of the additional district magistrate, Leh, on November 11 under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) had curtailed his freedom of movement and speech. He also sought an explanation for the deployment of around 20 to 22 armed police personnel at and around his residence.“The practical effect of their presence is that I am confined to my house,” Wangchuk said, asking the administration to clarify in writing whether he was free to leave his residence and, if not, under which legal provision he was being restrained.He said the order did not explicitly direct him to remain at home or mention house arrest, detention or confinement. According to Wangchuk, police personnel had orally instructed him to stay at his residence after taking him there on Wednesday evening.Wangchuk said he was at the proposed venue of a dharna at NDS Memorial Park in Leh around 8pm on November 11 when a group of policemen arrived and handed him a copy of the magistrate's order.He alleged that he was forcefully pushed into a vehicle by four masked men and taken to his residence at HIAL, reaching there around 8.40pm.He further alleged that he was not allowed to use his phone to inform his family or speak to a lawyer. He said around 20 to 22 armed police personnel had remained deployed at and around his residence since then.The activist also questioned the scope of the restrictions, saying the order did not specify where he could travel, during what hours, or whether he could leave home for work, medical treatment, worship or family obligations. He said the expression “any activity” in the order was vague and could prevent him from carrying out his ordinary occupation and day-to-day activities.The representation also sought a copy of the letter from the Senior Superintendent of Police, Leh, on which the magistrate's order was based, along with the material facts cited to justify the restrictions.Wangchuk said a dharna had been planned for November 12 to raise concerns over the advancement of the elections to December 4, the stalled dialogue between Ladakh representatives and the Union government, and the delay in making public the judicial inquiry commission report into the September 24, 2025 incidents.He said around 600 people had gathered for the protest on Thursday and that it had passed off peacefully, with no objection from the police. He argued that the gathering had not been stopped despite the order restricting unauthorised rallies and public gatherings.Questioning the administration's justification for the 60-day restrictions, Wangchuk said the electoral process was scheduled to conclude on December 8 and alleged that the action was intended to curtail his rights before the elections.He asked the administration to withdraw the order and the police deployment, and provide written clarification on the legal basis for restricting his movement.
Article Summary: Sonam Wangchuk alleges he has been placed under house arrest without a formal order after Ladakh imposed 60-day movement restrictions on him. He has written to the Ladakh administration seeking clarification over the order restricting his movement. Wangchuk said the order issued by the office of the additional district magistrate, Leh, on November 11 had curtailed his freedom of movement and speech.

Article Title: 'From armed struggle to people's politics': Ex-Maoist leader Deoji outlines new path, seeks release of jailed cadres
Article Text:
Thippiri Tirupathi alias Devji ruled out entering politcs for now

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

HYDERABAD: Surrendered CPI(Maoist) politburo member Thippiri Thirupathi alias Deoji, who was de-facto chief of the outfit after general secretary Namballa Keshav Rao was killed in May 2025, has decided to embrace democratic politics and raise people-centric issues in an open and legal manner. He has, however, ruled out entering electoral politics just yet.Currently studying law in a college in Hyderabad, Deoji wants to repurpose CPI(Maoist) into the party vehicle for carrying out his political plans. For this, he has demanded that the ban on CPI(Maoist) be lifted and even agreed on the need to rewrite the outfit’s political document to revise its tactics and strategy from “seizing power through armed struggle” to “people’s politics”.“The current circumstances are not conducive to continuing armed struggle...so we have decided to shun violence, illegal and secret activities and take up open and lawful political activity. In politics, our central agenda shall be to build an oppression and exploitation-free society...we will agitate for people’s rights and organise protests,” he stated in an exclusive interview to TOI more than 8 months after he surrendered before the Telangana police and joined the mainstream.Deoji said lifting of ban on CPI(Maoist) will give him an established platform to practice politics. However, if the ban is not reviewed anytime soon, he is open to floating an alternative political outfit. Apart from ending the UAPA ban on CPI(Maoist) and its fronts, the surrendered leader demanded that the Maoists still in jails should be freed. Though the state govts are reviewing non-serious cases against Maoists, Deoji is opposed to a distinction being drawn between serious and non-serious offences. “A blanket political call must be taken to drop cases against Maoists, irrespective of the gravity,” he said and even sought similar leniency for the 10 Maoists awarded death sentence for the Jhiram Ghati massacre.The Central govt, as per sources, has consistently opposed a “general amnesty” to Maoists. An NIA court had recently convicted and awarded death sentence to 10 Maoists in the case relating to the May 2013 Jhiram Ghati attack, which had killed 27 people including top Congress leaders in Chhattisgarh.Deoji revealed that the armed Naxal movement was severely hit due to sustained, decisive operations undertaken by the Central forces between Jan 2024 and March 2026, which literally “locked-in” the CPI(Maoist) leaders and cadres in Dandakaranya. Though the politburo and central committee leaders had, at their last meeting in August 2024, agreed to revise tactics — like disbanding the bigger formations like PLGA, operating in small teams, asking cadres to move out of Dandakaranya and focusing on working among the people — these could not be implemented as the leadership and cadres were encircled and overwhelmed by well-equipped counter-Naxal forces.“Our leaders, including general secretary Nambala Keshav Rao alias Basavaraju, were killed. Weapons were seized and cadres got concentrated in one place. This crushed our movement,” he revealed.Deoji said Mallojula Venugopal Rao alias Sonu surrendered without any go-ahead from the CPI(Maoist) leadership. “This triggered a chain reaction and we were unable to arrest the wave of surrenders,” he said.The August 2024 meeting of the apex Maoist leadership was attended by Basavaraju, former general secretary Ganpathy, politburo members Deoji and Sonu and central committee members Malla Raji Reddy alias Sangram, Kadari Satyanarayana Reddy alias Kosa, Katta Ramachandra Reddy and Ramdher.Basavaraju, Kosa and Katta Ramachandra Reddy were later killed by the counter-Naxal forces. The remaining leaders surrendered.
Article Summary: CPI(Maoist) politburo member Thippiri Thirupathi alias Deoji was de-facto chief of the outfit after general secretary Namballa Keshav Rao was killed in May 2025. He has decided to embrace democratic politics and raise people-centric issues in an open and legal manner. But he has, however, ruled out entering electoral politics just yet.

Article Title: 'Attempts to instigate public': Sonam Wangchuk faces 60-day restrictions on movement in Leh amid opposition to polls
Article Text:

Opposition to poll schedule

NEW DELHI: The Ladakh administration has imposed restrictions on climate activist Sonam Wangchuk ’s movement in Leh for 60 days, citing concerns over public order and the peaceful conduct of the ongoing electoral process.An order issued by the office of the additional district magistrate, Leh, on Wednesday said the restrictions were based on a report submitted by the senior superintendent of police, Leh, on November 11.The police officer had sought preventive measures against Wangchuk, alleging that his activities and previous conduct, including attempts to "mobilise and instigate" the public, had affected public order in the district.The order said there was apprehension that Wangchuk’s future programmes, demonstrations, hunger strikes and public gatherings could again disturb public peace and tranquillity. It also cited the possibility of such activities affecting elections to the Municipal Committee, Panchayats and the Ladakh Autonomous Hill Development Council (LAHDC), Leh.Invoking Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, the administration directed Wangchuk not to engage in activities or organise or participate in any unauthorised rally, procession or public gathering that could lead to a breach of public peace, disturb tranquillity or obstruct the ongoing electoral process in Leh district.The restrictions will take immediate effect and remain in force for 60 days, unless withdrawn or modified earlier in accordance with the law. The order also noted that the Model Code of Conduct is already in force in the district following directions from the State Election Commission and the Chief Electoral Officer, Ladakh.The order comes amid opposition from Ladakhi leaders, including Wangchuk, to the administration's decision to hold municipal and hill council elections during the winter months.On Wednesday, Wangchuk, along with Ladakh MP Mohmad Haneefa, Leh Apex Body (LAB) co-chairman Chering Dorjay Lakrook and Kargil Democratic Alliance (KDA) leaders, appealed to President Droupadi Murmu, Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union home minister Amit Shah to intervene and defer the polls.Calling it an “SOS call from Ladakh”, the leaders argued that severe winter conditions and the absence of a significant section of the population from the Union territory could affect voter participation.Wangchuk questioned the decision to hold elections when temperatures in parts of Ladakh can fall below minus 30 degrees Celsius and snowfall is expected in December. He also claimed that many residents, including students, are outside the region.“Ladakh is known as the world’s coldest inhabited place. The weather forecast for Dec indicates snowfall. How will elections be conducted in such conditions? Half of the population is outside Ladakh, while students are already studying in different cities. When Leh, Kargil and other areas are nearly empty, why are you holding elections?” he said.The leaders have argued that May or June would be a more suitable time for the polls to ensure wider participation. Haneefa said he had raised concerns about winter elections with the Ladakh lieutenant governor, while Lakrook described holding elections during peak winter as unheard of in the region.The municipal polls are scheduled for November 23, while the LAHDC election in Kargil is scheduled for December 4.
Article Summary: Ladakh administration imposes restrictions on climate activist Sonam Wangchuk’s movement in Leh for 60 days. Order cites concerns over public order and the peaceful conduct of the ongoing electoral process. Order comes amid opposition from Ladakhi leaders, including Wangchuk, to the administration's decision to hold municipal and hill council elections during the winter months.

NEW DELHI: A copy of veteran Congress leader Sonia Gandhi 's recently released memoir was burnt by families of the victims of the 1984 anti-Sikh riots and members of the Delhi Sikh Gurdwara Management Committee at Rakab Ganj Gurdwara on Thursday in protest against her account of the violence in which thousands of Sikhs were killed.In her memoir, Sonia writes that while her husband and former prime minister Rajiv Gandhi 's "heart held no bigotry or rancour", he was thrust into a moment in history when governance had failed, paving the way for barbarism.Recounting the events following the assassination of then prime minister Indira Gandhi, Sonia writes that news of her killing spread rapidly. NEW DELHI: A Kuki woman was killed and another person injured in a gunfight between suspected rival militant groups in Manipur’s Kangpokpi district on Thursday, officials said.The exchange of fire broke out around 11 am in an area between Taphou Kuki village in Kangpokpi district and Kailengjang in neighbouring Senapati district.Following the gunfight, a woman from Taphou Kuki village, who was working in a nearby field, was found shot dead. The victim, identified as Nengboi Chonglo, was reportedly holding a sickle when she was found.Her body was subsequently recovered by local residents and security personnel.The injured person, a man, was rushed to a private hospital in Kangpokpi district.The incident comes days after two Kuki youths, who went missing from the vicinity of Taphou Kuki village on October 28, were found dead in Senapati district on November 1.The killings triggered protests by the Kangpokpi-based Committee on Tribal Unity (COTU), which staged a sit-in demonstration at the district headquarters over what it termed an "unsatisfactory response to the organisation's charter of demands" concerning the abduction and killing of the two youths.COTU has demanded that Taphou Kuki village be brought under the jurisdiction of Kangpokpi district police instead of the Senapati district police station, which currently exercises jurisdiction over the area.According to Manipur Police ADGP (Law and Order) Lhari Dorjee Lhatoo, the state government was considering transferring the case to the National Investigation Agency (NIA)."The Manipur government's proposal to hand over the case to the NIA is at an advanced stage, and necessary orders are awaited," he had said on Tuesday.The ethnic conflict between the Meitei and Kuki communities, which erupted in Manipur in May 2023, continues, having claimed hundreds of lives and displaced thousands of people.

European foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas on Friday warned that Europe must not fall into Russia's "traps" as it prepares to join negotiations aimed at ending the war in Ukraine, insisting that securing a ceasefire must remain the immediate priority.According to AFP, speaking to reporters ahead of an EU summit in Dublin, Kallas cautioned against allowing discussions to shift towards Moscow's demands over Europe's security arrangements before the fighting stops."First we need a ceasefire. If we start to talk about what Russia is asking regarding the security architecture, we actually walk into the traps that Russia is setting us, which is that we divert the attention away from that there is no ceasefire," she said.Her remarks came a day after US special envoy Steve Witkoff indicated that European representatives would be included in the next round of Ukraine peace negotiations following his meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin at the Kremlin on Thursday.Putin said Russia had never opposed dialogue with European countries, arguing that European governments had themselves broken off direct engagement with Moscow.However, he warned that any foreign troops deployed in Ukraine after a peace agreement would be considered legitimate targets by Russia.The latest diplomatic developments followed two days of US-mediated talks between Russian and Ukrainian delegations in Abu Dhabi.The discussions marked the first direct negotiations between the two sides in nine months and resulted in progress on a prisoner exchange, but failed to resolve major differences over territorial issues and a possible ceasefire.

US intelligence officials reportedly suspect her of having links to Chinese intelligence services, an allegation that has added a national security dimension to the matter.The Wall Street Journal reported that Alice Huang was the woman referred to in a letter Jensen Huang sent to Nvidia employees, in which he acknowledged being unfaithful to his wife and apologised for violating her trust.Huang co-founded Nvidia in 1993 and transformed it into one of the world's leading suppliers of artificial intelligence chips, becoming one of the most prominent figures in the global AI industry.

MANDYA: A Mandya woman presumed murdered seven years ago has resurfaced alive, exposing serious lapses in the investigation that led to a man being charged with her ‘murder’ and jailed for two-and-a-half years.The man, Rajesh, now 36, who secured bail in 2024, has alleged that police tortured him into confessing to a crime he did not commit.Police registered a murder case and arrested Rajesh, relying primarily on the fact that Manju had made her last call borrowing the phone from Rajesh, a stranger, while at a bus stop shortly before she went missing.The case brings back memories of one Suresh from Kodagu, who was similarly accused of ‘murder’ and incarcerated for more than two years following his wife Mallige’s disappearance – until she resurfaced in April 2025.In the current case, Manju, now 36, who went missing from Pandavapura in 2019, was traced in Nagamangala Thursday after Rajesh’s advocate Natesh received a tip-off about her.In her statement to police, Manju reportedly said she had left home voluntarily because her family was forcing her into a marriage against her wishes and had since married another man and settled down. She also said she did not even know Rajesh.Police have initiated a fresh inquiry into her disappearance and the subsequent ‘murder’ probe. Superintendent of police Shobharani confirmed that Manju was placed in a women’s shelter home.Rajesh, a resident of Ragimuddanahalli village in Pandavapura taluk, Mandya, told reporters police inspector Prabhakar subjected him to custodial torture – including electric shocks to his private parts – to extract a confession.Fearing that his family would also be implicated, he claimed, he admitted to the ‘murder’ despite not being involved in it. He remained in prison for nearly two-and-a-half years before securing bail in Feb 2024.The case began in 2019 when Manju’s father, Nagaraju, lodged a missing-person complaint at Pandavapura police station. In 2021, he filed a murder complaint, claiming that two persons, Anantha Padmanabha and Gurukumara, had told him that Rajesh had confessed to killing his daughter and throwing her body into the Cauvery River
Article Summary: Manju, a woman missing since 2019, has been located alive, revealing major failures in the investigation. The man, Rajesh, now 36, who secured bail in 2024, has alleged that police tortured him into confessing to a crime he did not commit. Police have initiated a fresh inquiry into her disappearance and the subsequent ‘murder’ probe.

Article Title: 'Road is full of potholes': Back from Italy, woman whose Thar killed LIC employee breaks silence
Article Text:
The 24-year-old was granted bail last week after the incident.

What happened on the day of the accident

What the accused's lawyer said

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines





LUCKNOW: A 24-year-old woman who allegedly ran over and killed a 55-year-old LIC agent with her Mahindra Thar in Kanpur has claimed that she "panicked" during the incident and "pressed" the accelerator instead of the brake.Geeta Sachan, who was allegedly driving the SUV, said she swerved to avoid people on the road but lost control of the vehicle.She also claimed that she was not under the influence of alcohol or any other substance and that the car was not travelling at high speed."The road is full of potholes—we usually avoid taking that route. I was driving when, seeing someone approaching from the left, I panicked and swerved to the right. As I swerved, there were two women travelling in that direction. I swerved back to the left to avoid them, but by then, they (the victim) hadn’t managed to move out of the way.""In panic, I pressed the accelerator instead of the brake. My car hit them and then went on to collide with something else... I was not under any influence. If I had been going at a high speed, the airbags would have deployed—but they didn’t, because the car wasn’t moving fast," Geeta said.The 24-year-old was granted bail last week after the incident, which took place on Saturday evening in the Awas Vikas 3 area of Kalyanpur.Geeta is pursuing her studies in Italy and returned home for Diwali.The victim, Santosh Singh Chauhan, was returning home after stepping out to buy a saree for his wife. He was barely 500 metres from his house when the SUV rammed into his scooter.The impact dragged Chauhan and his vehicle for around 20 metres before the Thar crashed into a green area outside a house.The SUV first struck the house of Professor Kailash before crashing into the boundary wall of Anita Mahevan's house, residents said.Chauhan, a resident of Swaraj Nagar in Panki, was identified by his son, Rahul. He said his father had left home telling the family that he would be back shortly.Sachan's lawyer, Advocate Anant Kumar Sharma, maintained that the incident was an accident and that his client had no intention of causing anyone's death."The accused neither knew the deceased nor any of their relatives; and certainly, she had no intention whatsoever for anyone to die. Due to factors such as the presence of numerous potholes on the roads and the lack of street lighting, this incident occurred as an accident.""The charges should have reflected the nature of an accident. The sections invoked by the police were incorrect; consequently, the remand application was rejected, and she was released upon furnishing a personal bond of Rs 25,000 and an undertaking," Sharma said.He also urged people not to make inappropriate remarks about the court's order, saying those who disagreed with it could pursue legal remedies."I strongly urge the public to refrain from making inappropriate remarks about court orders. If individuals disagree with a verdict, legal avenues are available to them—such as filing a revision petition or an appeal," he said.
Article Summary: Geeta Sachan, who was allegedly driving the SUV, said she swerved to avoid people on the road but lost control of the vehicle. She also claimed that she was not under the influence of alcohol or any other substance and that the car was not travelling at high speed. The victim, Santosh Singh Chauhan, was returning home after stepping out to buy a saree for his wife.

Article Title: Lucknow Development Authority demolishes illegal construction of triple murder accused's home

Triple murder accused’s house being razed by LDA team

LUCKNOW: Days after the murder of three members of a family in Lucknow's Brahmani Tola, the Lucknow Development Authority (LDA) on Thursday began demolishing the house of prime accused Rishabh Shukla after declaring the structure illegal.Officials said action was also being taken against unauthorised portions of two other properties linked to the case.The demolition was carried out following a court order issued to LDA over complaints of illegal construction and encroachment on Nazul land. The building owner was given the prescribed time to comply before the demolition action was initiated.Shukla has been arrested along with five others in connection with the killings of Shivaji Tiwari, Shivendra Tiwari alias Shambhu and Suyash Tiwari in the Naubasta locality of Brahmani Tola under the Saadatganj police station limits.The building was constructed without a sanctioned layout plan. During an inspection, the construction was found to be completely unauthorised, and the family members failed to produce an approved building plan or any other supporting documents,” LDA secretary Gyanendra Verma said.An LDA enforcement team had sealed Shukla’s residence on Oct 27 with the assistance of a heavy police contingent. On Thursday, a large police force was deployed in the locality to maintain law and order as bulldozers razed the illegal portions in the presence of senior LDA officials.
Article Summary: The demolition was carried out following a court order issued to LDA over complaints of illegal construction and encroachment on Nazul land. Rishabh Shukla has been arrested along with five others in connection with the killings of three members of a family.

Article Title: 'We'll get you a new mother': Retired railway employee slits wife’s throat, surrenders with daughters

A retired railway loco pilot is accused of murdering his wife, Pooja Devi, in Bihar's Munger district.

JAMALPUR: “Your mother is dead, we’ll get you a new mother,” a 55-year-old retired railway loco pilot allegedly told his two young daughters after slitting his 28-year-old wife’s throat at their rented home in Bihar’s Munger district late Wednesday night.The accused later took the girls, aged eight and five, to the local police station and surrendered.The victim, identified as Pooja Devi, was found dead inside a locked room at the couple’s residence near Sadar Bazaar in Jamalpur town, under Adarsh Jamalpur police station limits. Police recovered the suspected murder weapon from the spot and sent the body for post-mortem examination.According to preliminary investigations, the accused allegedly locked the two children in a separate room before attacking his wife. After the murder, he locked the room containing her body, covered it with a sheet and took the children to the police station, where he surrendered.Police suspect the murder was triggered by the accused’s suspicion that Pooja was involved in an extramarital relationship. Investigators, however, said all possible angles were being examined.Meanwhile, Pooja’s family alleged that she had faced domestic harassment and dowry-related torture for several years.Her brother, Shubham, said the family was informed by police late Wednesday night about the murder and the accused’s surrender.“We spoke to Pooja just two days ago, but she did not mention any serious problem,” Shubham said. He alleged that the accused and some of his relatives had been harassing and assaulting her for nearly five years. He also claimed that the accused frequently questioned her character because of the age difference between the couple.Pooja, a resident of Ishakchak in Bhagalpur, married the accused in 2015. The couple had been living in a rented house near Sadar Bazaar with their two daughters.Jamalpur SHO Pankaj Kumar said police were investigating the motive and circumstances behind the crime. The accused has been arrested, and further legal action will be taken after completion of the necessary procedures and registration of an FIR based on the family’s complaint.
Article Summary: A retired railway loco pilot is accused of murdering his wife, Pooja Devi, in Bihar's Munger district. Police suspect the murder was triggered by the accused's suspicion that Pooja was involved in an extramarital relationship. Article Title: 'Ask him which judges belong to BJP and which to Trinamool', Calcutta HC tells Abhishek Banerjee’s counsel
Article Text:
Trinamool MP Abhishek Banerjee (File Photo)

KOLKATA: Trinamool MP Abhishek Banerjee ’s alleged comments that “some” high court judges owe allegiance to Bengal’s governing party, made after a reported attack on his Kalighat home last Saturday, prompted Calcutta High Court to tell his lawyer on Thursday, “Your client is very intelligent. Please ask him to give a list of judges who belong to BJP and who belong to Trinamool.”Justice Krishna Rao made the observation after additional advocate general (AAG) Bilwadal Bhattacharyya highlighted Banerjee’s comments, reported in news media, and demanded that criminal contempt proceedings be started against him. Bhattacharya read out Banerjee’s alleged comments on judiciary’s link with the governing party and its impact on verdicts.The MP, whose security cover has been downgraded by the state govt, allegedly made the comments after his house was attacked late on Saturday by around 50 people armed with sticks fitted with nails.Appealing against reduction in Banerjee’s security, his counsel, Shoeb Alam, submitted before Justice Rao, “This is the speech of a man who is exasperated and is running around for your lordship’s protection. Running from pillar to post to get some protection for his family and him, and for no fault of his but because the party he is affiliated with lost elections.Because of which, not one but six attacks have taken place… This is a clear case of breakdown of rule of law. ”Justice Rao said, “If you are facing difficulty, court is there. If not this court, then you go to another forum. It (the comment on judiciary’s alleged political link) can be taken if it’s a general public, but if it’s an educated person who is an MP and holding a good post in a political party. He is not a layman who doesn’t know what he is telling before the media. He can say anything against any person. But on a matter pending before the court…”The judge reserved his order on the plea against reduction in Banerjee’s security cover and the subsequent six attacks on him, the latest of which was reported last Saturday. Justice Rao repeatedly asked the state why the six attacks on Banerjee were not taken into account by the govt after the May 29 review meeting, which decided on scaling down his security from Z+ to X.When AAG Bhattacharyya submitted that the threat perception of all MPs would be reassessed at the next review meeting, scheduled for Nov-end, Justice Rao said, “You (the BJP govt) have to wait for six months? Your new regime came on May 10, immediately you reduced. There’s no problem. But once you have received representation (from Banerjee), why are you dragging the matter? Why are you waiting for six months?”Banerjee’s counsel submitted that considering the spate of violence since the announcement of the assembly poll results, his client feared he could be assassinated. He flagged multiple actions by the state, including removal of police kiosks outside Banerjee’s home, and alleged that the govt had acted mala fide.While the MP’s counsel said only two personal security officers had been guarding his client since May 12, the AAG submitted that three PSOs were tasked with protecting Banerjee. He clarified that Z+ security was usually provided to the CM, governor and other persons facing threats.Most MPs, he said, are given X security cover.“Banerjee’s residence continues to remain under high-grade security. He is being provided with three PSOs. Most of the incident petitions are pending. The right of a person to claim a particular class of security cannot be a matter of right,” the AAG submitted.
Article Summary: Trinamool MP Abhishek Banerjee allegedly made the comments after his house was attacked late on Saturday by around 50 people armed with sticks fitted with nails. Calcutta High Court: “Your client is very intelligent. Please ask him to give a list of judges who belong to BJP and who. belong to Trinamool.”

Article Title: 'Prove it': BJP MLA Maithili Thakur rejects land grabbing allegations against family
Article Text:
BJP MLA from Alinagar Maithili Thakur (File Photo)

PATNA: BJP MLA from Alinagar Maithili Thakur has denied allegations of land encroachment against her father, Ramesh Thakur, and challenged complainants to substantiate their claims before the authorities.Villagers have accused Ramesh of illegally occupying religious sites, govt land, roads and private property. The complaints concern the shrine of Gram Devta Tiwari Baba, a Radha-Krishna temple and a Dihbar. He has also been accused of filling a drainage channel originating from a local pond and constructing a caretaker’s room.Villager Ram Autar Mishra has alleged encroachment on his land, while Ramday Devi claimed excavation along her property’s boundary had endangered trees. Residents have also raised concerns over soil excavation along the boundaries of other private plots.RJD MLA Bhai Virendra accused Maithili’s family of using political influence to grab land. He alleged land grabbing and intimidation had become a pattern among NDA leaders and criticised the media for giving greater prominence to ruling alliance statements than those of the opposition.Rejecting the allegations, Maithili said her family had valid land documents and described the claims circulating on social media over the past two days as baseless.She said a house was being built on land known as ‘Pokhar Bhinda’, where village elders regularly gather and extend their support."I, too, only started seeing these posts two days ago. Land mafias, grabbing land, taking away the poor's rights—I'm reading all these things. These false allegations against our family are baseless. It upsets me deeply to hear that people are writing such things. If there's anything to this, ask the local circle officer.If an allegation is being made, what is it based on? Prove it... I'm very concerned that people are using such strong language—what is it based on?. .. Baseless rumours are being spread," she said.She urged complainants to approach the circle officer, DCLR or other competent authorities with evidence instead of making allegations online.Circle officer Alok Kumar said an application had been received from villagers and both parties had been summoned to a ‘janata darbar’. Further action would be taken after hearing their submissions.
Article Summary: BJP MLA from Alinagar Maithili Thakur has denied allegations of land encroachment against her father. Villagers have accused Ramesh of illegally occupying religious sites, govt land, roads and private property. RJD MLA Bhai Virendra accused Maithilia’s family of using political influence to grab land.

Article Title: Woman buys Rs 1,755 pressure cooker, finds rice and dal remain uncooked despite 3-4 whistles; consumer commission orders refund, Rs 12,000 compensation and Rs 3,000 costs, imposes Rs 21,000 penalty on
Article Text:
AI Generated Image Used For Representational Purpose Only

HYDERABAD: A pressure cooker bought for Rs 1,755 was supposed to make everyday cooking easier. Instead, a woman in Visakhapatnam found that rice remained partially uncooked even after three to four whistles. When the same problem persisted while preparing dal the following day, she approached the seller for help. The dispute eventually landed before a consumer commission, which ordered the store, dealer and manufacturer to pay her Rs 16,755.The Visakhapatnam District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission ruled that the woman was entitled to a refund of the product's cost, along with compensation and litigation expenses, after finding deficiencies in the services provided by the three parties.The commission, presided over by Gudla Tanuja, with members Varri Krishna Murthy and Rahimunnisa Begum, passed the order on October 31. The woman had purchased a four-litre deep-pan pressure cooker from a store for Rs 1,755, paying through UPI. She said she first noticed the problem when she used it to cook rice on the day of purchase. Despite allowing the cooker to function for the prescribed three to four whistles, the rice was only partially cooked.An attempt to prepare dal the next day yielded the same result, according to her complaint. She then contacted the store, alleging that its staff responded insensitively and asked her to approach the company's service centre. However, citing her age and physical limitations, she said she could not visit the centre. The store subsequently collected the cooker from her and issued a service bill for its repair. But the woman maintained that she wanted a replacement rather than a repair. The company later informed her that it had instructed the dealer to replace the appliance, but the dealer had not acted on the instruction, the commission noted.The store and the dealer maintained that the cooker had been examined by service personnel, who had even shared a video demonstrating that it was working properly. Their lawyers told the commission that the woman had refused an offer to accompany her to the service centre for a demonstration. They also argued that she had insisted on a replacement despite the appliance being in working condition and was seeking an excessive amount as compensation.The store and dealer further contended that she had not submitted an expert opinion or technical report to establish a manufacturing defect. They also accused her of threatening litigation and claiming to have connections with consumer commission personnel. The manufacturer, meanwhile, argued that its warranty obligations were limited to repairing or replacing products with inherent manufacturing defects. It maintained that the cooker had undergone operational testing and was found to be functioning properly.The commission observed that the store, dealer and manufacturer had failed to produce the warranty terms before it. It also questioned their reliance on a proposed replacement as a goodwill gesture, asking why such an offer would have been made if the appliance had no problem. The bench held that the woman was entitled to a refund as a consumer exercising her legal rights under the Consumer Protection Act, and not merely because the company was willing to offer a goodwill replacement.It also took exception to the allegations that she had used purported connections within the commission to threaten the store and dealer. Describing the remarks as defamatory, the commission said they amounted to an attempt to tarnish the institution's image and included derogatory comments about the complainant.The commission directed the store, dealer and manufacturer to refund the Rs 1,755 paid for the cooker, pay Rs 12,000 as compensation for deficiency in service and bear Rs 3,000 towards litigation costs. Separately, the store and dealer were directed to pay a penalty of Rs 21,000 to the Andhra Pradesh State Legal Services Authority in Amaravati for making what the commission described as baseless allegations about its functioning.
Article Summary: A woman in Visakhapatnam found that rice remained partially uncooked even after three to four whistles. The dispute eventually landed before a consumer commission, which ordered the store, dealer and manufacturer to pay her Rs 16,755. The commission ruled that the woman was entitled to a refund of the product's cost.

Article Title: How scrap dealer lured ex-Tech Mahindra regional head Paramjeet Dhankar to his death: 'Brother, brother, please’, 14 bullets, magazine change'
Article Text:
CCTV footage shows the sequence of events that led to the cold-blooded murder on Nov 7.

How past disputes culminated in Faridabad shooting

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines





FARIDABAD: “Dhankar sahab, please come out for a moment. I need to park my car,” scrap dealer Mohan Sharma urged his neighbour Paramjeet Dhankar, a senior vice-president with Singapore-based FPT Software who had returned to his Faridabad home just a day earlier to attend his nephew’s wedding.Minutes later, as the two walked outside the main gate, Sharma pumped nine bullets into Dhankar, reports. As the senior IT executive staggered towards the road, trying to escape, Sharma pursued him, continued firing and even changed his magazine as bullets ran out. He then shouted, “Happy Diwali. I will kill everyone today.”Sharma did not stop even after Dhankar slumped to the ground. He fired at his son, who escaped behind parked cars. The incident took place just 500m from the police commissioner’s office.CCTV footage shows the sequence of events that led to the cold-blooded murder on Nov 7. According to police, Sharma, a scrap dealer, fired 14 rounds from his licensed pistol. Dhankar, an ex-Asia Pacific head of Tech Mahindra, died before he could be wheeled into hospital.The killing followed weeks of friction between the two families, who lived in the same building in Sector 21C and shared its parking area.Dhankar’s family occupied the ground floor, Sharma lived on the second, and two other families occupied the first and top floors. With four households competing for space, parking had repeatedly triggered arguments, a relative told TOI.According to police, there was also tension between the two families over Sharma’s pet dog. Dhankar’s son had objected to the dog defecating in the common parking area.An earlier confrontation on Oct 22 had further soured relations. Sharma allegedly damaged the gate of Dhankar’s house, an incident captured on the family’s CCTV cameras. The family gave the footage to police, who called Sharma to the station and allegedly reprimanded him.But another confrontation took place at the local police station on the day of the murder. Sources said Dhankar’s friends and aides confronted Sharma, abused and manhandled him. Both sides returned home at 6pm. But the humiliation is likely to have fuelled his anger.Later that evening, Sharma rang the bell at Dhankar’s house and repeatedly urged him to come downstairs and move his car. Dhankar came down with his son, Shaurya. In the footage, Sharma is heard addressing him as “Dhankar sahab” and repeatedly saying, “Brother, brother, brother, please.”The exchange turned hostile. When Dhankar suggested he did not want to continue the conversation, Shaurya began moving towards the staircase. Sharma allegedly stopped him and asked him to return. He then pulled out his licensed .45 ACP pistol, fitted with an extended magazine, and fired.Dhankar tried to get away, staggering from the garage towards the road. Sharma dashed towards him, firing as he went. As Dhankar fell outside the building, his wife rushed out. But Sharma continued firing and changed the magazine. He then threatened the family and called out to them to come outside.Dhankar returned from Singapore on Nov 5 for his nephew’s wedding in Meerut.Police arrested Sharma near DLF Chowk in Ballabhgarh the next day and seized the weapon. A case was registered against him under BNS sections 103 (murder), 109 (attempt to murder) and 61(2) (criminal conspiracy).
Article Summary: Mohan Sharma, a scrap dealer, fired 14 rounds from his licensed pistol. Paramjeet Dhankar, an ex-Asia Pacific head of Tech Mahindra, died before he could be wheeled into hospital. The killing followed weeks of friction between the two families who lived in the same building in Sector 21C.

Article Title: Curtains drawn on NCP(SP)-NCP merger after Ajit Pawar's death, received no fresh proposal: Supriya Sule
Article Text:
Supriya Sule, the working president of NCP (SP), has ruled out any potential merger between the party factions

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines





PUNE: NCP (SP) working president Supriya Sule on Thursday ruled out any merger between the Sharad Pawar-led NCP and the rival party led by the late Ajit Pawar , saying she had decided to “draw the curtains” on the issue following her cousin’s death and had received no fresh merger proposal.Supriya’s remarks come amid renewed efforts by several NCP seniors to revive merger discussions and speculation over possible rapprochement between the two parties. On Wednesday, NCP president Sunetra Pawar declined to clarify the possibility of a merger between the two NCPs, saying matters would become clear at the appropriate time.“Discussions on the merger were on when Ajit Pawar was alive, and the entire world knew about them. A video of one such meeting held on Jan 17 was also circulated in the media,” Supriya said.“The day my cousin died, and following the developments that unfolded a few days after his death, I decided to draw the curtains on the issue of merger. I do not think I should speak much on the topic. It ended with my cousin’s death,” she said.After Ajit Pawar’s death in a plane crash on Jan 28, senior leaders of his party had denied holding any meetings with the Sharad Pawar-led party to discuss a merger.However, state NCP president Sunil Tatkare recently said he was aware of the talks and claimed that the merger would have taken place had Ajit Pawar been alive.Tatkare and state minister Hasan Mushrif on Thursday said they would soon meet Sharad Pawarin Mumbai, fuelling further speculation about efforts to bring the two parties together.“I will meet Pawar Saheb to enquire about his health when I visit Mumbai. He is our mentor, and I do not think there is anything wrong with any member of our party meeting him for personal reasons,” Tatkare said.On the merger issue, Mushrif said the decision would be taken by his party chief, Sunetra Pawar. “We will abide by the decision Sunetra Pawar takes on the merger,” he said.Responding to Shiv Sena neta Sanjay Shirsat’s suggestion that a third faction could emerge in NCP, Mushrif said attempts were being made to weaken the party after Ajit Pawar’s death. Mushrif added that he would approach deputy CM Eknath Shinde and urge him to caution members of his party (Shiv Sena) against targeting NCP.
Article Summary: Supriya Sule, the working president of NCP (SP), has ruled out any potential merger between the party factions. Her remarks come amid renewed efforts by several NCP seniors to revive merger discussions and speculation over possible rapprochement between the two parties.

Article Title: PM Modi to inaugurate Bengaluru Metro Pink Line, attend yoga institution's 50th anniversary celebrations
Article Text:
Bengaluru makes preparations for Prime Minister Narendra Modi's visit to inaugurate the Namma Metro Pink Line. (File pic)

BENGALURU: Prime Minister Narendra Modi is scheduled to visit Bengaluru on Friday to inaugurate the Namma Metro Pink Line and attend the Golden Jubilee celebrations of Prashanti Kutiram, which also mark the birth centenary of author HV Sheshadri.The programme at S-VYASA University, organised by the S-VYASA Registered Society, is scheduled to begin at 10am. RSS Sarkaryavah Dattatreya Hosabale will attend as the distinguished guest, while Karnataka governor Sudha Yadav, chief minister DK Shivakumar and Ahn Byeong-Gu, mayor of South Korea's Miryang City, will be guests of honour.The celebrations mark 50 years of Prashanti Kutiram, which is known for its work in yoga research. H.R. Nagendra, president of VYASA Society, said the institution was developing a specialised research laboratory, named Ritambhara, to study higher dimensions of yoga, including Samadhi."We are celebrating the Golden Jubilee of 50 years of our service at Prashanti Kutiram. We are known for research in the world. We are going further to develop the most unique research lab called Ritambhara to track the higher dimensions of yoga to what we call Samadhi," Nagendra told news agency ANI.He also announced the launch of S-VYASA's Thiruvananthapuram campus to coincide with the Prime Minister's visit. Nagendra acknowledged the contributions of the institution's faculty, students and alumni and invited people to join the celebrations online.Meanwhile, the institution will organise a free artificial limb fitting camp to commemorate Sheshadri's birth centenary. Prem Bhandari, chief adviser for international affairs at S-VYASA, said 1,000 people would be provided with artificial limbs under the initiative.Bhandari, who represents Jaipur Foot USA, said the decision was taken after discussions with the organisation's founder, Padma Bhushan D.R. Mehta.He also recalled Modi's association with the initiative, saying the Prime Minister had inaugurated one of its camps in 2016 at his request.Bhandari said he was also working towards establishing an S-VYASA centre in New York, as part of efforts to expand the institution's international presence.(With agency inputs)
Article Summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi is scheduled to visit Bengaluru on Friday. He will inaugurate the Namma Metro Pink Line and attend the Golden Jubilee celebrations of Prashanti Kutiram. The programme at S-VYASA University will also mark the birth centenary of author HV Sheshadri.

Article Title: Brent crude falls over $1 as Trump signals fresh US strikes on Iran are unlikely
Article Text:
Crude oil eases after Trump's remarks

Trump warns Iran despite ruling out fresh strikes

Hormuz caught in chokehold

Oil prices opened lower on Monday, with Brent crude briefly shedding more than $1 a barrel.The dip comes after US President Donald Trump said that fresh American strikes on Iran were “highly unlikely” if negotiations between the two countries made progress.Brent crude futures fell 52 cents, or 0.53%, to $97.80 a barrel. US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures slipped 15 cents, or 0.17%, to $90.68 a barrel.Trump's comments offered an indication that the US could avoid another round of military action against Iran, provided Tehran agreed to what he described as a strong deal. However, reports from both countries of shipping being hit in and around the Strait of Hormuz kept concerns over disruptions to the strategic waterway alive."It depends on whether or not they sign a very strong agreement," Trump told CNN in a phone interview. "The answer is, highly unlikely it's going to be necessary."In a 20-minute telephone interview with CNN, Trump repeated five times that renewed military intervention was unlikely if Iran made tangible progress in negotiations over its nuclear programme and the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz.The US president, however, warned that Washington had identified 38 Iranian bridges that could be destroyed within an hour if further military action became necessary."We have 38 bridges in our site that we can knock down in literally one hour. They’ll all be down," Trump told CNN.The remarks come amid continued disruption to crude oil supplies through the Strait of Hormuz, which has now lasted for over eight months. The disruption has affected refinery operations across major Asian and Middle Eastern economies.According to the US Energy Information Administration (EIA), global refinery activity fell sharply in the second quarter of 2026 after the Middle East conflict broke out.Data from energy intelligence firm Kpler showed that global refinery inputs dropped by 4.8 million barrels per day (b/d), or 6%, in April-June compared with the previous quarter. However, they recovered by 1.8 million b/d in the third quarter as refiners adapted to changing trade flows and alternative supply routes.Countries that rely heavily on crude supplies passing through the Strait of Hormuz were among the worst affected.China saw the biggest decline, with refinery inputs falling by 2.1 million b/d in the second quarter and a further 0.8 million b/d in the third quarter.India, South Korea and Japan together recorded a drop of more than 1 million b/d in crude oil inputs in the second quarter. Their combined inputs recovered by 0.8 million b/d in the following quarter.
Article Summary: Brent crude futures fell 52 cents, or 0.53%, to $97.80 a barrel. US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures slipped 15 cents, to $90.68 a barrels. US President Donald Trump said fresh American strikes on Iran were “highly unlikely” if negotiations between the two countries made progress.

Article Title: Sheikh Hasina seeks new passport for Bangladesh return, Dhaka says not 'to a terrorist'

Death sentence and legal proceedings

NEW DELHI: Former Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina has formally sought a new passport and national identity card (NID), taking a step towards her planned return from India in December.The information comes from a Monday letter sent by Hasina’s lawyers to the acting high commissioner at Bangladesh's embassy in Delhi, Preeti Rahman, Reuters reported.Hasina's lawyers at London-based Matrix Chambers requested the issuance of fresh documents. They cited the reported cancellation of her existing passport and NID by Bangladesh's interim government and other authorities."In view of the reported revocation of her existing Bangladeshi passport and National Identity Card (NID) by the Interim Government and other authorities, I respectfully request that you take the necessary steps to issue a new Bangladeshi passport and National Identity Card for our client," the lawyers wrote.The letter urged the authorities to process the applications "expeditiously", citing Hasina's Bangladeshi nationality and the country's "obligations arising under international human rights instruments".However, Bangladesh denied Hasina’s request, stating that the country does not provide "passport to a terrorist"."She is a fugitive criminal. We have an active extradition treaty with India. We want her handed over," Bangladesh state minister for foreign affairs, Humaiun Kobir, told reporters."Should we treat her like an ordinary commercial traveller and tell her ​to come and visit her ​in-laws’ residence?" Kobir jibed.According to Reuters, the request is the clearest indication yet that Hasina is taking steps to act on her stated intention to return in December, more than two years after a deadly uprising forced her from power. Her return could reignite political and legal tensions as Bangladesh attempts to restore stability and her Awami League party remains banned.Hasina intends to return and surrender before a court. Her aides said on Monday that the date would be announced after the completion of various formalities.Last week, the exiled leader the Associated Press she would prefer dying in her own land, among her own people.“If death is my destiny, I would rather die on the soil of my own country, among my own people,” Hasina said.In November 2025, Bangladesh's war-crimes tribunal sentenced Hasina to death in absentia for ordering a crackdown on the student-led uprising. She has denied the charges, rejected the verdict and questioned the legitimacy of the trial.The crackdown killed hundreds of protesters and left thousands injured. According to United Nations data cited by the Associated Press, nearly 1,400 people were killed during the unrest.Bangladesh has repeatedly sought Hasina's extradition from India. New Delhi has said the request is being examined through legal channels.Hasina's Awami League was Bangladesh's largest political party before it was banned following her removal from office. Several of its leaders and members have since been jailed, while others have gone into self-imposed exile in India and elsewhere.Having served as Prime Minister for 20 years across multiple terms, Hasina retains support among sections of the population. Her return could deepen political divisions as the country continues to deal with the aftermath of the upheaval.It could also have implications for Bangladesh's strained relationship with India, which deteriorated sharply after New Delhi gave the former prime minister refuge.
Article Summary: Sheikh Hasina has formally sought a new passport and national identity card (NID) The request is reportedly the clearest indication yet that Hasina is taking steps to act on her stated intention to return in December. Bangladesh denied Hasina’s request, stating that the country does not provide "passport to a terrorist"

Article Title: ‘I don’t care’: How Jensen Huang’s last hours as Nvidia CEO unfolded
Article Text:
The Nvidia co-founder, once known for his relentless energy and extraordinary attention to detail, appeared broken by the mounting controversy
