Jensen Huang's final hours as Nvidia chief executive were marked by exhaustion, resignation and an apparent surrender after weeks of fighting to hold on to his position amid allegations of extramarital affairs and links to a suspected Chinese spy, Bloomberg reported.According to Bloomberg, citing a person familiar with the situation, Huang's usual take-charge demeanour had disappeared. Instead, he had started using phrases such as "whatever" and "I don't careThe Nvidia co-founder, once known for his relentless energy and extraordinary attention to detail, appeared broken by the mounting controversy. Less than a week after admiting infidelity and being embroiled in an alleged espionage plot by a Chinese spy, Huang's resistance had seemingly collapsed by late Wednesday night.The developments came despite an intervention by US President Donald Trump, who called Huang on Tuesday and urged him to fight for his position, The New York Times reported, citing two people briefed on the conversation. Huang, however, resigned on Thursday.The crisis had intensified following reports of Huang's alleged relationships with multiple women, including Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang, whom US authorities suspect of having links to Beijing's intelligence services.The New York Times also reported that Huang had a second alleged affair with an Nvidia executive who reported directly to him. Further reports identified the executive as company vice-president Kimberly Powell.The controversy has also raised questions about Nvidia's business and its standing amid growing scrutiny of the artificial intelligence sector. The company's shares fell 4.3% on Thursday after an opening drop of around 14%, recovering some ground during the session.The stock has lost 30.5% since reaching a record high on October 6.Nvidia's troubles have also added to pressure on the broader technology market, given its significant contribution to gains in the S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite.Meanwhile, the controversy has spilled into Washington, with the White House reportedly weighing whether to remove Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick over his handling of technology exports to China. The issue has drawn renewed scrutiny amid questions over the administration's response to national security risks involving advanced US chips.
Article Summary: Jensen Huang's final hours as Nvidia chief executive were marked by exhaustion, resignation and an apparent surrender. He resigned amid allegations of extramarital affairs and links to a suspected Chinese spy. Huang's usual take- charge demeanour had disappeared. Instead, he had started using phrases such as "whatever" and "I don't care"

Article Title: Uranium stockpile remains unverified: Iran refuses nuclear inspections under US military threat, tells UN watchdog
Article Text:
Nuclear tensions flare as Iran defies fresh US threats, refuses to halt uranium enrichment or surrender stockpile.

Why Iran is refusing nuclear inspections

What is the concern over Iran's uranium stockpile?

Isfahan nuclear facility raises fresh concerns

Iran objects to US reward offer for nuclear information

Bushehr remains the only inspected nuclear facility

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Iran has told the UN nuclear watchdog that discussions on resuming inspections of its nuclear facilities cannot proceed while the country faces threats of further US military attacks, particularly against its nuclear infrastructure. Tehran has also warned that normal monitoring cannot resume until what it describes as the root causes of the current crisis are addressed.The position was conveyed in a letter to the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA), detailed in a confidential report circulated among member states on Friday and seen by The Associated Press. The development comes as the agency remains unable to inspect several Iranian nuclear facilities damaged in Israeli and US strikes in June 2025 or independently verify the country's stockpile of highly enriched uranium.In its communication, Iran referred to “a series of persistent, explicit, and public threats by the President of the United States of America … to commit further acts of armed aggression” against Iran “particularly targeting its nuclear facilities.”Iran said the situation won't resolve “until the root causes of the present situation are addressed and the essential requirements for normal safeguards implementation are restored," the report added.Despite its refusal to resume full inspections under the current circumstances, Tehran reaffirmed its “firm commitment to resume full implementation of its safeguards obligations as soon as the relevant legal and actual conditions permit it.”The IAEA, however, warned that the prolonged absence of inspections and lack of information about Iran's nuclear material posed an urgent proliferation concern. It said it was “fully prepared to resume its safeguards activities in Iran at short notice.”The dispute over nuclear inspections intensified after Israel and the US launched a 12-day military campaign against Iran in June 2025, targeting several nuclear facilities and other strategic installations.The strikes damaged or destroyed parts of Iran's nuclear infrastructure, but the full extent of the damage and the status of nuclear material stored at the affected locations remain unclear.Iran has since denied IAEA inspectors access to nuclear facilities affected by the strikes, preventing the agency from verifying their condition and accounting for the country's enriched uranium stockpile.Tehran argues that the military attacks and continued threats against its nuclear infrastructure have created conditions in which normal inspections cannot be conducted.The IAEA, meanwhile, maintains that it must be able to verify Iran's nuclear material and facilities under its safeguards obligations.The agency has encouraged Tehran to “consider technical and gradual measures” that could facilitate the return of inspectors and restore normal monitoring arrangements.One of the biggest concerns for the IAEA is Iran's stockpile of uranium enriched to 60% purity, which is close to the 90% enrichment level generally associated with weapons-grade uranium.According to the agency's last verified estimate, Iran possessed 440.9 kg (972 pounds) of uranium enriched to up to 60% purity before the June 2025 strikes.IAEA Director General Rafael Grossi had warned that the stockpile could potentially provide enough material for as many as 10 nuclear bombs if Iran decided to weaponise its programme. However, this does not mean that Tehran possesses nuclear weapons or has taken a decision to develop them.Under the agency's safeguards guidelines, such highly enriched nuclear material should normally be verified every month.The prolonged absence of inspections has left the IAEA unable to establish the current quantity, location and condition of the stockpile.The agency has described the lack of access and information about Iran's nuclear material as “a matter of proliferation concern" that “needs to be rectified with the utmost urgency.”The IAEA has also expressed “increasing concern” over Iran's Isfahan Fuel Enrichment Plant, a facility that Tehran first notified to the agency in June 2025, shortly before the Israeli and US military strikes began.IAEA inspectors were scheduled to visit the facility on June 13, 2025, but the inspection was cancelled after the military campaign began.In its latest report, the agency said it “does not know” the site's “exact location or whether it contains nuclear material."The lack of access has prevented inspectors from establishing whether the facility contains nuclear material or whether enrichment activities have taken place there.The Isfahan facility is particularly important because of continuing uncertainty over the location of Iran's enriched uranium and the extent of damage to its nuclear infrastructure.The IAEA has repeatedly called on Tehran to provide information about its nuclear facilities and allow inspectors to resume verification activities.Iran has also raised concerns over a recent US offer of a reward of up to $20 million in exchange for information about its nuclear programme.In a letter to the IAEA, Tehran stressed the importance of maintaining the “confidentiality” of the agency's activities and ensuring that information relating to Iran's nuclear programme is not “disclosed, misused or exploited.”The objection comes amid concerns in Tehran that sensitive information gathered during international inspections could be used for purposes beyond nuclear monitoring.The IAEA has maintained that safeguarding confidential information is an essential part of its verification activities.The Bushehr nuclear power plant is the only facility in Iran inspected by the IAEA since June 2025, according to the agency's report.Inspectors visited the facility between September 12 and 15.The Russian-built reactor currently operating at Bushehr uses uranium supplied by Russia and enriched to 4.5%, a level used for civilian nuclear power generation.However, inspections at Bushehr have not resolved the agency's concerns over access to other nuclear facilities, particularly those affected by military strikes.Iran has long maintained that its nuclear programme is peaceful and intended for civilian purposes. However, the IAEA and Western countries have said Tehran had an organised nuclear weapons programme until 2003.The latest standoff over inspections adds to tensions between Iran and the US, with the fate of the country's enriched uranium stockpile and the future of international monitoring remaining unresolved.
Article Summary: Iran tells UN nuclear watchdog that discussions on resuming inspections of its nuclear facilities cannot proceed while the country faces threats of further US military attacks. Tehran has also warned that normal monitoring cannot resume until what it describes as the root causes of the current crisis are addressed. The position was conveyed in a letter to the International Atomic Energy Agency.

Article Title: Flávio Bolsonaro says he will run again, denies fleeing Brazil after defeat
Article Text:
File photo: Brazilian senator Flavio Bolsonaro sits for an interview

Brazilian senator Flavio Bolsonaro has brushed aside criticism over his departure for the United States after losing last month's presidential election, saying he is prepared to run again.In an interview with Reuters in Washington on Thursday, Bolsonaro dismissed accusations, including those made by Lula, that he had fled Brazil after the October 25 election. He described the “fugitive” label as an attempt to discredit him and said he believed leaving the country had been necessary.The move has nevertheless drawn public disapproval. A Quaest opinion poll found that 62% of Brazilians disapproved of his decision to leave after Lula defeated him by more than four million votes.Bolsonaro, the son of former president Jair Bolsonaro, said he expected economic difficulties to undermine Lula's fourth term, arguing that high household debt, weak business investment and what he called an unfair legal system were putting pressure on Brazil.“If a new electoral race emerges, I am ready to return,” he said, adding that he intended to contest it under the banner of the right-wing Liberal Party. He offered few details about his standing within the party or how he planned to rebuild support after leaving Brazil.The senator also repeated allegations of electoral fraud without providing evidence, despite Brazil's electoral court declaring Lula the winner and Bolsonaro's political allies accepting the result. He acknowledged that legal challenges to the outcome were unlikely to succeed, but accused the judiciary of being influenced by the government.Asked about an earlier letter in which he had initially described himself as “president-elect” before changing the wording to “leader”, Bolsonaro avoided directly claiming the title and instead shifted responsibility of his words onto the people who had voted for him in the elections. “To millions of Brazilians, that's who I am,” he said.US stay and questions over his departureBolsonaro's visit to Washington comes as questions remain over how he and his family travelled to the United States. Brazil's Supreme Court had ordered him to surrender his passport before his departure, citing money-laundering investigations and concerns that he could flee. He travelled with his family through Argentina and Ecuador, but declined to tell Reuters who helped arrange the journey.US secretary of state Marco Rubio said on October 31 that Washington had not been directly involved. However, Reuters and other media outlets subsequently reported that White House official Jason Miller had helped organise the trip. Bolsonaro declined to discuss the circumstances of his departure.He said he was not afraid of being investigated but believed he would not receive fair treatment in Brazil. He also said he had not met US president Donald Trump since arriving in Florida and denied that Washington or any other foreign government had interfered in Brazil's election.Bolsonaro expressed gratitude to Trump, who said on October 31 that the senator could remain in the United States for as long as he wanted. Trump had called Brazil's election “a disgrace”, although outside observers described the vote as free and fair.In a separate appearance at a right-wing gathering at Trump's Mar-a-Lago property last week, Bolsonaro told attendees that his electoral defeat was not “the end for Brazil”. His effort to remain politically relevant has, however, drawn questions from analysts about whether he weakened his position by leaving the country rather than leading the opposition from Brazil.Bolsonaro said he had not decided whether his family would remain in Florida. He added that he had the financial means to support himself in the United States as a senator, lawyer and businessman, but declined to say whether he had transferred money there.
Article Summary: Bolsonaro dismissed accusations, including those made by Lula, that he had fled Brazil after the October 25 election. He described the “fugitive” label as an attempt to discredit him and said he believed leaving the country had been necessary.

Article Title: Gavin Newsom to run for US president in 2028? California governor sets January deadline
Article Text:
California Governor Gavin Newsom

What did Newsom say about Trump's midterm setback?

Will Kamala Harris 's decision affect Newsom's plans?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

California Governor Gavin Newsom has said he will decide by early January whether to enter the race for the 2028 US presidential election, bringing his long-discussed White House ambitions closer to a formal decision.Newsom announced his timeline during a visit to Turkey for the COP31 international climate conference, where he also criticised President Donald Trump and described the recent midterm election results as a rebuke of the Republican leader.“I’ll make the determination at the beginning of the year, so we’ll spend the next few weeks with the family and make a decision early January,” Newsom told Turkey's Anadolu news agency.The announcement comes as speculation grows over potential Democratic contenders for the next presidential election. Newsom, who has increasingly positioned himself as a prominent critic of Trump, has repeatedly hinted at a possible White House bid without formally declaring his candidacy.During the interview, Newsom described the election results as an “historic rebuke” of Trump's presidency and said Democrats now had an obligation to offer voters a positive alternative.“Donald Trump’s presidency as we know it ended last week in the US,” he said, adding that those who succeeded in the elections must now focus on governing and providing a new agenda for the Democratic Party.Newsom also used his Turkey visit to highlight California's climate policies and criticise Trump's decision to withdraw from international climate commitments.He met Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva to discuss expanding climate cooperation between California and Brazil and finalised a new climate agreement with Portugal, according to his office. He also visited a forestry training centre to exchange lessons on wildfire management.Newsom has previously indicated that former Vice President Kamala Harris's potential entry into the 2028 presidential race could influence his decision.In September, he told CNN that he would not contest the Democratic nomination if Harris decided to run.“I wouldn’t run if she ran,” Newsom said during an interview with CNN's Jake Tapper in Montana.He described a potential contest between the two Democrats as “mutual assured destruction”, citing their overlapping networks of supporters and political allies.Newsom has also said that support from his family, including his four children, would be essential before making a final decision.“If they’re not on board, that’s a nonstarter,” he said.However, his presidential prospects remain uncertain. Recent prediction market figures cited by US media suggested that his chances of securing the Democratic nomination had fallen to around 7 per cent following the midterm election results.Newsom's January announcement could therefore provide an early indication of how the Democratic field for the 2028 presidential election is shaping up.
Article Summary: California Governor Gavin Newsom will decide by early January whether to enter the race for the 2028 US presidential election. Newsom announced his timeline during a visit to Turkey for the COP31 international climate conference. He has repeatedly hinted at a possible White House bid without formally declaring his candidacy.

Article Title: Delhi inaugurates 11-km Chhath Ghat along Munak Canal, calls it country's longest
Article Text:
Delhi inaugurated an 11-km-long Chhath Ghat along both banks of the Munak Canal.

Ghat to host other cultural celebrations

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines





NEW DELHI: Delhi chief minister Rekha Gupta and BJP national president Nitin Nabin on Thursday inaugurated an 11-km-long Chhath Ghat along both banks of the Munak Canal in North Delhi, ahead of festival.The Delhi government has called it as the country's longest Chhath Ghat, developed to provide better facilities to devotees from the Purvanchal community and other parts of the city.Union minister of state Harsh Malhotra, Delhi ministers Parvesh Sahib Singh, Manjinder Singh Sirsa and Kapil Mishra, MP Praveen Khandelwal and several MLAs were also present at the inauguration.The project, being developed at an estimated cost of Rs 115.29 crore, involves the redevelopment of an approximately 11-km stretch along both sides of the canal. It includes the construction of the Chhath Ghat, service roads along the canal, bridges, road widening and beautification work.The government said the development would transform the previously neglected stretch into a cleaner public space with improved infrastructure and facilities. Steps, lighting arrangements and parks are also being developed for devotees.Addressing the gathering, Nabin said the project reflected the government's recognition of the religious beliefs and cultural identity of the Purvanchal community, whose members have contributed to the development of Delhi.He said Chhath was not merely a religious ritual but a festival rooted in purity, devotion, discipline and gratitude towards nature. Devotees offer arghya to the setting and rising Sun, while the festival brings people together across social divisions.Nabin said the development of the ghat would allow people from Purvanchal and Bihar to celebrate Chhath in Delhi with dignity and access to proper facilities. He added that the initiative reflected respect for the faith and traditions of different sections of society.Chief minister Rekha Gupta said the area around the Munak Canal had remained neglected for years and residents had been waiting for a dedicated facility where devotees could perform Chhath rituals.She said the project was taken up as a priority after the BJP government came to power in Delhi. The chief minister added that the development was part of the government's efforts to improve infrastructure across the capital."Chhath celebrations in Delhi will be grander and more divine this year than last year," Gupta said. She also said she would visit different ghats, celebrate the festival with devotees and offer arghya to the Sun God.Malhotra said the project was significant not only for improving infrastructure but also for preserving Delhi's cultural and religious heritage. He said the ghat would serve as a venue for cultural, social and public activities throughout the year, beyond Chhath celebrations.He added that mothers and other devotees observing the fast would be able to offer arghya with access to better facilities.Irrigation and flood control minister Parvesh Sahib Singh described the facility as Delhi's longest Chhath Ghat and the first of its kind in the country to be developed along a canal. He said the Purvanchal community had played a significant role in building Delhi and that providing devotees with a dedicated place to perform their rituals was a matter of dignity and respect.Meanwhile, culture minister Kapil Mishra said Chhath celebrations were being organised at 1,400 ghats across Delhi this year. He claimed that better arrangements had been made for devotees at the ghats along the Yamuna as well.The government said the Munak Canal redevelopment would also provide organised spaces for other religious and cultural events, including Durga Puja and Ganesh Puja.
Article Summary: The Delhi government has called it as the country's longest Chhath Ghat. It was developed to provide better facilities to devotees from the Purvanchal community. Devotees offer arghya to the setting and rising Sun, while the festival brings people together across social divisions.
